decisions.reason: The source permits reordering power-connector pins while requiring the matching main-board connector to use the same order; it does not change I2C speed, cabling, pull-ups, or signal conditioning.
Changing the permitted pin order does not alter the selected connector types or any component sourceability or cost constraint.
The source concerns the interboard power connector's pin order, not the battery connector's placement, orientation, spacing, or mounting-hole clearance.
Permission to arrange connector pins to suit the layout does not modify the board dimensions, aspect ratio, mounting holes, enclosure fit, USB-C position, or other mechanical constraints.
The source and preceding question concern the interboard power connector carrying +5V and 3.3V, not the separate three-pin battery connector interface.
Reordering physical pins on a matched interboard connector does not change the switched 5V rail's voltage, control GPIO, enable behavior, converter, pull-down, loads, or operating pattern.
The connector pin-order decision does not change the task-local obligation to review assembly settings, pricing, or component availability.
